messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered for service=ingress-eastus3, symptom=5xx_surge, severity=page

pagerduty-bot: Pager assigned to @sre_oncall (rotation: infra-rotations) — please acknowledge

sre_oncall: acked — looking

maya: I'm on it. seeing a big spike in 502/504 from envoy at edge eastus3. Grafana: error_rate ~ 18% on avg across ALB fronting envoy.

dave: Confirmed. NLB metrics show increased connection resets and high active connections on nodepool-a. Could be upstream cannonball from new deployment?

carla: No deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot: `deploy-bot: no recent deploys to ingress namespace` :eyes:

maya: grabbing envoy logs from one pod:
```
[2026-03-15T10:02:12Z] envoy error: upstream reset: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-15T10:02:13Z] 502 response to client: connect failed upstream
```

maya: kubectl get pods -n ingress shows many envoy pods in Ready state but high restart counts on envoy-proxy-2.

carla: Could be an NLB backend node problem — running `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn tg-ingress-eastus3` shows ~10% unhealthy in targetgroup.

infra-rotations: Paging note: customer impact suspected for ~5% of production traffic in eastus3, primarily small API customers and some regionally routed clients. Escalate to oncall lead if >10%

sre_oncall: Trying quick mitigation: switching ALB weights to divert 30% traffic to eu-west1 as a temporary relief. Running script: `./scripts/shift-alb-weight --from=alb-eastus3 --to=alb-eu-west1 --pct=30`

maya: started increase of envoy replicas from 6 -> 12 in ingress-ns, to absorb bursts. Command: `kubectl scale deploy envoy --replicas=12 -n ingress`

dave: I also bumped NLB connection timeout and reduced proxy_read_timeout on envoy to drop stale conns. Config snippet:
```
proxy_read_timeout: 10s
keepalive_timeout: 30s
```

carla: Running health re-checks on nodes — one EC2 instance in az-eastus3b shows network interface errors. Opening a ticket with cloud provider and marking it draining in ASG. `asg detach-instance --instance i-0abc123 --should-decrement-desired=false`

infra-rotations: Good call to drain rather than terminate. If node is flapping, that will reduce resets quickly.

sre_oncall: After initial weight shift + scale + drain: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 6% in the last 3m. Still seeing intermittent resets.

maya: Observed a pattern: traffic hitting a particular AZ presented 10x higher error rate. Suggest performing AZ-level failover (route 100% of eastus3 weight to other regions) if it trends upward.

dave: I can update routing policy in Route53 to move eastus3 weight to eu-west1 progressively. Will do + watch latency impacts.

deploy-bot: Canary deploys: no canaries running.

carla: Customer impact update: internal monitoring flagged 12 customers with >50% request failures — proactively opened support tickets and emailed affected customers.

infra-rotations: Status update we should record: initial spike 10:02Z, drained node 10:08Z, scaled envoys 10:09Z, ALB weight 30% -> eu-west1 10:11Z, errors drop to 6% by 10:14Z.

sre_oncall: I'm going to hold the mitigations and continue observing for 20m. If stable, we gradually return weights and uncordon new node.

maya: adding temporary alert runbook note: if 5xx > 10% for >5m AND NLB connection_reset_rate > threshold, escalate to SRE lead and start region weight failover play.

dave: Also added per-target connection tracking to detect conntrack exhaustion on nodepool. `curl http://metrics/conntrack | grep nodepool-a` showed saturating counts on two nodes. We patched kernel conntrack limits on the draining node as band-aid.

carla: Cloud provider responded: NIC on i-0abc123 had transient packet drops; they replaced instance backing host and reported network heal at 10:23Z.

sre_oncall: Thanks. We're seeing errors sub-1% now in eastus3 after full node replacement and gradual weight return. Rolling back ALB weight in 10% increments.

infra-rotations: Closing steps: ensure postmortem, assign follow-ups: verify conntrack tuning is applied to autoscaling launch template (owner: dave), add runbook step for AZ failover (owner: maya), customer comms follow-up (owner: carla).

carla: Noted for support: we'll send a summary to impacted customers with timeline and mitigation actions.

deploy-bot: Incident resolved in monitoring at 10:37Z — automated uptime check green.

sre_oncall: marking incident as resolved, creating incident ticket for retrospective. Thanks team :thumbsup:

maya: +1 — saved runbook snippets into #incidents-docs for the postmortem.

carla: closing thread; will post final customer notification when CT is ready. :email:
